messages:
devon: FYI we got an updated NVIDIA driver advisory (525.85.x -> 525.91.x) with a couple CVE fixes. Need to plan a rolling patch + verification runbook. Who can own canary + KMS signature checks?

alex: I can own the canary deployment this weekend. plan: 1-node staging + 2 canaries in dedicated pool, run smoke + perf.

sara: KMS question first — are we validating vendor RPM/DEB signatures against our KMS/HSM policy, or just rpm --checksig / dpkg-sig? We should require vendor-signed + our internal attestation if we repackage.

devon: Good point. My proposal: verify vendor signature on the package, then a secondary internal signature (cosign) signed by our infra key stored in HSM. If either check fails, abort rollout.

jamie: For the canary tests, add these quick checks: `nvidia-smi -q` for driver health, `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` for errors, run a small cuDNN conv workload, and a NCCL allreduce smoke with 2 GPUs. Capture load/unload errors.

alex: Agree. I'll script those. Also add model-level sanity: run a short decode on our bert-serve endpoint and verify no significant latency spike (>20%) and no inference errors.

sec-bot: CVE-2025-XXXX: driver module exposes /proc info that could leak kernel addresses. Severity: HIGH. Recommended: vendor patch available. Impact: local privilege escalation vector.

devon: That CVE makes this P0 for host images used by customer-dedicated pools. Need patch in both hosted and dedicated images. We should prioritize Dedicated first (SLA customers).

alex: Rollout schedule proposal: Thursday 03:00-06:00 UTC for staging/canary, Friday 02:00-08:00 UTC for dedicated rolling patch (small batches), Sat 00:00-06:00 UTC for host pool (wider). Notify support + account execs for Dedicated.

sara: Ops checklist for each batch: 1) drain new allocations from node, 2) stop running containers, 3) install driver pkg, 4) reboot if kernel modules replaced, 5) run jamie smoke tests, 6) run perf harness for 10m, 7) mark healthy/fallback.

devon: Fallback plan: if smoke fails, re-install previous driver version from our internal artifact repo and restart services. Ensure we keep old driver packages available for 72h.

jamie: Compatibility catch: cuDNN and NCCL ABI sometimes break across minor driver bumps. Before patching prod, we'll test existing pinned cuDNN/cuda combinations in a staging matrix: CUDA 11.8/12.0 + cuDNN 8.3/8.4 + NCCL 2.14. If any mismatch, we either pin an older driver image for that model route or rebuild container with matching libs.

alex: Quick commands I'll use in the smoke script: ```bash
# verify signature
rpm --checksig /tmp/NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64-525.91.run || exit 1
# kernel module
modinfo nvidia | grep -E 'version|srcversion'
# cuDNN check
python -c "import ctypes; print(ctypes.CDLL('libcudnn.so.8').cudnnGetVersion())" || true
```

sec-bot: Add audit logging requirement: all driver install attempts and signature verification results must be emitted to our audit pipeline (syslog -> secure ELK) with request_id. That satisfies compliance for Dedicated.

devon: Good. Also: KMS ops question — can infra sign the cosign artifact non-interactively with HSM? If not, we need manual step in the runbook.

sara: We have an HSM-backed cosign workflow for automated CI; infra-ops will need to ensure the service account has signing privileges. I'll add a preflight to confirm key access.

alex: I'll put the canary scripts + smoke harness in the runbook repo and tag with `nvdriver-1765432100`. Will push PR tonight.

devon: Communication plan: short status to #incidents if canaries fail, otherwise a summary in #product and email to Dedicated customers post-maintenance. Please add SLA owner to the notice.

jamie: One more: during canary install, capture kernel oops logs and upload to private S3 bucket path: s3://redwood-devops/driver-patches/1765432100/ so we can triage quickly.

alex: ack. Will run and report back with timestamps + artifact links. :thumbsup:

devon: Thanks all. Action items: alex (canary + scripts), jamie (smoke matrix + upload hook), sara (KMS key preflight + compliance logging), devon (customer comms + rollback policy). If anyone hits blockers ping me or escalate to oncall.
